newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese banks slash numbers of branches.
newsitem.headline: Chinese banks slash numbers of branches.

text.p: China's state-owned banks, lumbered by bad debt and inefficiency, have slashed their numbers of branches in recent years after a growth war in the 1980s, the Xinhua news agency said in a report.

Last year, China's largest bank, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China closed 1,669 offices and downsized 1,091 county-level branches, Xinhua said. It did not give the current number of branches.
The China Construction Bank last year merged or dismantled 1,928 local offices, it said.
The Bank of China, China's leading foreign exchange bank, shut down 163 domestic offices that were losing money or performing poorly, Xinhua said.
However, it opened more outlets abraod, increasing the number of overseas branches or joint ventures to 533.

The Agricultural Bank of China, which saw 10 billion yuan in losses in property and capital in 1996 as the government moved to further reform the rural banking industry, shut or merged more than 3,000 offices in the countryside, Xinhua said.
It opened more than 1,800 urban branches, it said.

In 1996, the Agricultural Development Bank of China was hived off to create a policy bank offering state-subsidised loans for grain purchases and poverty-relief, leaving the Agricultural Bank to restructure as a commercial bank, it said.
However, central bank governor Dai Xianglong cited some of the difficulties state banks face in becoming real commercial entities.
Dai told a meeting last week that Chinese bankers should no longer operate banks as government institutions and urged local governments to stop interfering in bank operations.
China's four main state banks have for years operated as review by local election officials, almost 47,000 of the 59,000 petition signatures submitted were valid. Petitioners needed about 28,000.
To be sure, the petition review did not settle the dispute between city officials and critics of the expansion plan.
The city agreed to a $60 million plan in 1995 to expand the stadium to 70,000 seats. But in December, the city amended the contract, adding $18 million to the project.
Golding will seek to place the $18 million amendment to the expansion plan on the city ballot "as quickly as legally possible," her spokeswoman said.
